# Dyalog sessions


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Import [`Apl`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl)
and
[`AplError`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#aplerror)
from `basedpl.dyalog`. Sessions return Dyalog output or JSON-converted
Python values, not BPL arrays. Importing this module does not start
Dyalog or register notebook magics.

Install Dyalog separately. The examples use a local interpreter and run
with `nbdev-test --flags dyalog`. The default test run skips them.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
```

## Connecting

[`find_dyalog`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#find_dyalog)
checks the command path and standard macOS/Linux installation locations.
Pass `dyalog=` to
[`Apl`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl) to choose
another executable.
[`Apl`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl) uses
`timeout` only during the startup handshake, not while evaluating code.

RIDE uses length-prefixed messages over a local socket.
[`ride_run`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#ride_run)
collects session output until Dyalog is ready for another expression.
[`Apl.run`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl.run)
handles interactive and incomplete-input prompts.

## Evaluating APL

`run` returns session output as text. Assignments persist across calls:

``` python
dyalog = Apl()
out = dyalog.run('x←1 2 3\n+/x')
test_eq(out.strip(), '6')
out
```

    '6\n'

Calling a session returns
[`AplOut`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/magics.html#aplout),
the same text with notebook display support. A silent assignment returns
`None`:

``` python
test_is(dyalog('quiet←7'), None)
dyalog('2×x')
```

<pre class="bpl_out">2 4 6</pre>

## Python values

`pyval` uses Dyalog’s JSON conversion. Scalars become Python values and
numeric arrays become lists. `basedpl.reference` calls `pyval` for its
reference checks:

``` python
test_eq(dyalog.pyval('+/x'), 6)
matrix = dyalog.pyval('2 3⍴⍳6')
test_eq(matrix, [[1,2,3], [4,5,6]])
matrix
```

    [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]

Use square brackets to evaluate an APL expression or assign a
JSON-compatible Python value. Single quotes in strings are escaped for
APL:

``` python
dyalog['values'] = [3,1,4]
dyalog['message'] = "can't"
test_eq(dyalog['message'], "can't")
test_eq(dyalog['values'], [3,1,4])
dyalog['values']
```

    [3, 1, 4]

The callable returned by `fn` converts Python arguments through JSON and
evaluates the APL function expression on each call. Passing one argument
sets `⍵`, and passing two sets `⍺` and `⍵`:

``` python
mean = dyalog.fn('{(+/⍵)÷≢⍵}')
test_eq(mean([1,2,3]), 2)
add = dyalog.fn('+')
test_eq(add([1,2,3], 10), [11,12,13])
add([1,2,3], 10)
```

    [11, 12, 13]

## Errors and lifetime

`run` raises this module’s
[`AplError`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#aplerror)
for a Dyalog error, not `BplError`. Assignments that run before an error
stay in the session:

``` python
with expect_fail(AplError, contains='DOMAIN ERROR'): dyalog.run('saved←42 ⋄ 1÷0')
test_eq(dyalog['saved'], 42)
dyalog['saved']
```

    42

[`Apl.run`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl.run)
rejects interactive
[`⎕`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/quad.html) and `⍞`
input with
[`AplError`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#aplerror).
When Dyalog shows an incomplete-input prompt,
[`Apl.run`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl.run)
restarts the interpreter, losing the workspace, and raises
[`AplError`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#aplerror)
with `reset=True`.

Call `close()` when finished, or use
[`Apl`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/dyalog.html#apl) as a
context manager to close the session automatically:

``` python
dyalog.close()
with Apl() as reference: total = reference.pyval('+/⍳10')
test_eq(total, 55)
total
```

    55
